elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: Total external debt rises overall between 2015 and 2025. The printed endpoints are 577 in 2015 and 1,531 in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.description: The stacked bars break down 2025 external debt into public and publicly guaranteed and short-term debt, then by creditor type and selected creditors. Multilateral debt is the largest creditor type at US$913 million, followed by private creditors at US$495 million and bilateral creditors at US$122 million. Other multilateral is the largest named multilateral component at US$442 million; Kuwait is the smallest bilateral component at US$28 million.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show debt ratios from 2015 to 2025 against shaded percentile ranges. The printed 2025 ratios are highest for external debt / exports at 441% and lowest for debt service / GNI at 2%. External debt / GNI is shown falling by 8.1%, while the other three printed changes are positive.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: The left box, Official creditors, shows maturity of 18 years, grace period of 5 years and interest rate of 0.9%, with a small bar beneath each measure. The right box, Private creditors, lists the same three measures as '..' with empty bars. No private-creditor values are shown because the country had no new commitments in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
